chief_complaint: chronic dry cough, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and red tender bumps on shins for 2 months
hpi_details: 2-month history of a persistent, dry, irritating cough accompanied by progressive shortness of breath when climbing stairs or walking uphill. Simultaneously, developed severe joint pains and swelling affecting both ankles and knees (symmetrical arthralgia), low-grade afternoon fevers, chronic exhaustion, and noticed multiple exquisitely tender, raised, erythematous nodules across the anterior aspects of both shins (erythema nodosum). Last week, noticed her eyes becoming painful, red, and sensitive to light (anterior uveitis). Denies weight loss, haemoptysis, night sweats, or occupational dust exposure.
ideas: thinks her body's immune system is attacking her lungs and joints after a viral infection
concerns: worried she might have lymphoma or tuberculosis spreading through her chest
expectations: wants eye drops, joint pain killers, and a chest scan to diagnose the cause
medications: ibuprofen 400mg TDS with minimal relief of joint/shin pain
social_hx: never smoked, drinks socially, secondary school teacher, married

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of sarcoidosis is essential for confirming the diagnosis, assessing organ involvement, and protecting vision and renal function.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Löfgren's syndrome (erythema nodosum + BHL + arthralgia) carries an excellent prognosis with spontaneous remission occurring in >80% of patients within 12 to 24 months without systemic steroids, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: chronic dry cough, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and red tender bumps on shins for 2 months

Key HPI features: 2-month history of a persistent, dry, irritating cough accompanied by progressive shortness of breath when climbing stairs or walking uphill. Simultaneously, developed severe joint pains and swelling affecting both ankles and knees (symmetrical arthralgia), low-grade afternoon fevers, chronic exhaustion, and noticed multiple exquisitely tender, raised, erythematous nodules across the anterior aspects of both shins (erythema nodosum). Last week, noticed her eyes becoming painful, red, and sensitive to light (anterior uveitis). Denies weight loss, haemoptysis, night sweats, or occupational dust exposure.

Objective/Exam findings: Examine shins: multiple tender, warm, red/violaceous nodules over bilateral anterior tibiae (erythema nodosum). Check joints: periarticular swelling and tenderness of bilateral ankles. Check eyes: ciliary flush, photophobia, and pupil irregularity (anterior uveitis -> requires urgent slit-lamp exam). Auscultation: lung fields clear or mild crackles. Erect Chest X-ray: classical Stage I / Stage II Sarcoidosis pattern -> symmetrical, potato-node Bilateral Hilar Lymphadenopathy (BHL) plus right paratracheal lymphadenopathy (Garland's triad), with or without reticulonodular parenchymal infiltrates. Bloods: Serum Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (S-ACE -> elevated in >60% of active cases), serum calcium elevated (hypercalcaemia due to unregulated 1-alpha-hydroxylase production of active Vitamin D by alveolar macrophages), 24-hour urinary calcium excretion elevated, FBC (lymphopenia). Spirometry / DLCO: normal or mild restrictive deficit with reduced DLCO. Diagnostic tissue confirmation: Endobronchial Ultrasound-guided Transbronchial Needle Aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) of hilar lymph nodes -> confirms non-caseating non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas with Schaumann bodies and asteroid bodies, with negative special stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi.
Current medications: ibuprofen 400mg TDS with minimal relief of joint/shin pain
common_misconceptions: Assuming that bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is diagnostic of sarcoidosis without excluding infection and malignancy when indicated.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Assuming sarcoidosis without considering infections, malignancy, and relevant occupational or environmental exposures.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring urgent ocular symptoms, hypercalcaemia, or progressive pulmonary impairment.
management_principles: Löfgren's syndrome (erythema nodosum + BHL + arthralgia) carries an excellent prognosis with spontaneous remission occurring in >80% of patients within 12 to 24 months without systemic steroids

Joint and skin symptoms may be managed with analgesia or anti-inflammatory treatment selected by the treating clinician after contraindication review; if NSAIDs already tried have given minimal relief (as in this patient), the treating clinician should consider dose/agent adjustment rather than simply repeating the same regimen.

Painful red eye, photophobia, or visual change requires same-day ophthalmology assessment; ophthalmic or systemic corticosteroids should be prescribed only by the relevant treating specialist, particularly given the excellent prognosis of Löfgren's syndrome without steroids for the pulmonary/joint manifestations alone.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 36F presents with 2-month classic Löfgren's syndrome triad: erythema nodosum on shins, bilateral ankle arthralgia, and dry cough/exertional dyspnoea, complicated by acute anterior uveitis.
reference_soap.objective: Examine shins: multiple tender, warm, red/violaceous nodules over bilateral anterior tibiae (erythema nodosum). Check joints: periarticular swelling and tenderness of bilateral ankles. Check eyes: ciliary flush, photophobia, and pupil irregularity (anterior uveitis -> requires urgent slit-lamp exam). Auscultation: lung fields clear or mild crackles. Erect Chest X-ray: classical Stage I / Stage II Sarcoidosis pattern -> symmetrical, potato-node Bilateral Hilar Lymphadenopathy (BHL) plus right paratracheal lymphadenopathy (Garland's triad), with or without reticulonodular parenchymal infiltrates. Bloods: Serum Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (S-ACE -> elevated in >60% of active cases), serum calcium elevated (hypercalcaemia due to unregulated 1-alpha-hydroxylase production of active Vitamin D by alveolar macrophages), 24-hour urinary calcium excretion elevated, FBC (lymphopenia). Spirometry / DLCO: normal or mild restrictive deficit with reduced DLCO. Diagnostic tissue confirmation: Endobronchial Ultrasound-guided Transbronchial Needle Aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) of hilar lymph nodes -> confirms non-caseating non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas with Schaumann bodies and asteroid bodies, with negative special stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi.
reference_soap.assessment: Systemic Sarcoidosis presenting with Löfgren's Syndrome (acute benign self-limiting phenotype) and acute anterior uveitis. DDx: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (differentiated by caseating/necrotizing granulomas and positive AFB stains), Hodgkin/Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (differentiated by asymmetric adenopathy and Reed-Sternberg cells), Berylliosis, Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
reference_soap.plan: Löfgren's syndrome (erythema nodosum + BHL + arthralgia) carries an excellent prognosis with spontaneous remission occurring in >80% of patients within 12 to 24 months without systemic steroids. For symptomatic joint and skin management, since ibuprofen has given only minimal relief, the treating clinician should consider adjusting the NSAID regimen (e.g., an alternative agent such as naproxen) after reviewing contraindications, rather than continuing the same dose. Given the acute anterior uveitis, arrange urgent same-day ophthalmology referral for slit-lamp assessment and topical steroid eye drops; systemic corticosteroids are reserved for severe uveitis or if progressive pulmonary impairment or hypercalcaemia develops, and should be prescribed only by the treating specialist. Arrange serial monitoring with repeat chest X-ray, spirometry/DLCO, and serum/urinary calcium as directed by the treating team.

learning_objectives: Identify the pathognomonic clinical triad of Löfgren's Syndrome: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, and ankle arthralgia
Correlate alveolar macrophage dysregulation with elevated Serum ACE levels and hypercalcaemia/hypercalciuria
Interpret EBUS-TBNA biopsy confirming non-caseating epithelioid granulomas while strictly ruling out caseating tuberculosis
Outline the excellent spontaneous remission trajectory (>80%) of Löfgren's syndrome while identifying strict steroid indications (uveitis/hypercalcaemia)

teaching.one_liner: A multisystem granulomatous disease that can present with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, arthritis, and uveitis.

must_ask.say: How long have the cough and breathlessness been present, and are they getting worse?
Have you developed tender red shin nodules, ankle swelling, or joint pain?
Have you had painful red eyes, light sensitivity, or any change in vision?
Have you had palpitations, fainting, facial weakness, kidney stones, or other new symptoms?
Have you been exposed to tuberculosis, beryllium, mould, birds, or medicines that can cause lung inflammation?
